presetSummaryBtn.description: Label for quick summary preset button

presetSummaryText.message:
Provide a concise executive summary of the attached document:

1. Overview: Core topic and objective in 1–2 sentences.
2. Key Takeaways: Top 3–4 essential findings or insights.
3. Bottom Line: Main implication or practical conclusion.
4. Limitations & Constraints: Key caveats, limitations, or scope boundaries in 1–2 sentences.

Keep it structured, clear, and scannable.
presetSummaryText.description: Text filled by quick summary preset button

presetPointsBtn.description: Label for key points preset button

presetPointsText.message:
Extract the key points from the attached document into structured bullet points:

• Core Insights: Most critical ideas, facts, or arguments.
• Evidence & Data: Specific figures, findings, or proof points.
• Practical Takeaways: Direct conclusions or actionable implications.
• Limitations & Constraints: Key caveats, limitations, or scope boundaries in 1–2 sentences.

Be specific, concise, and avoid generic filler.
presetPointsText.description: Text filled by key points preset button

presetPeerReviewBtn.description: Label for peer review preset button

presetPeerReviewText.message:
Act as an expert scientific researcher and critical peer reviewer. Read the attached research paper (or text provided below) and generate an in-depth, rigorous summary using the exact structure below. Rely strictly on the provided text; do not extrapolate, assume, or add external references.

1. Metadata
Title, Journal, & Year: [Extract]
Authors & Institutions: [Extract]

2. Research Core
Main Research Question/Objective: [1–2 sentences defining what the study aims to find out]
Core Hypothesis / Central Thesis: [What specific prediction or premise is tested]

3. Methodology & Data
Study Design: [e.g., randomized controlled trial, in vitro, observational, computational model]
Sample Size & Data Source: [Exact numbers, organisms, materials, or datasets used]
Analytical Approach: [Statistical tests or computational methods applied]

4. Key Findings & Evidence
Present the top 3–5 primary findings. For each finding, provide a short paraphrased summary followed by a direct verbatim quote (1–2 sentences) from the paper that supports it.

5. Limitations & Constraints
Methodological/Data Limitations: [Explicit constraints or unaddressed confounding variables noted by authors]
Generalizability: [Limits on where or to whom these findings apply]

6. Significance
Field Impact: [1 sentence on how this materially advances the discipline]
